title: Odd block runs and collapse under interval restriction
statement: Use the simplex and coordinate convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For r\geq0 and p,q\in\{-,+\}, let W_r(p,q) be the nonempty finite strings x=(x_0,\ldots,x_w) in \{0,\ldots,r+1\} with x_0=0 (respectively r+1) when p=- (respectively p=+), x_w=0 (respectively r+1) when q=- (respectively q=+), and successive inequalities alternating strictly, starting with < when p=- and with > when p=+. For 0\leq h\leq r, label each entry by \chi_h(j)=0 for j\leq h and \chi_h(j)=1 for j>h. Every maximal constant \chi_h-run in x has odd length. Put C_h(j)=\min(j,h+1) and D_h(j)=\max(j-h,0) on \{0,\ldots,r+1\}, and apply these maps entrywise. Then R(C_{h*}x) is obtained by replacing each maximal 1-run by one entry h+1, while leaving each 0-run unchanged, and R(D_{h*}x) is obtained by replacing each maximal 0-run by one entry 0, while replacing each maximal 1-run (x_i,\ldots,x_k) by its entrywise image (x_i-h,\ldots,x_k-h). No reduction crosses a run, and the surviving run order and alternating inequality directions are unchanged. For a finite word y, R(y) denotes the deterministic reduction obtained by repeatedly deleting the leftmost adjacent equal pair.

source.place: Riehl--Verity, Proposition 3.2.2 proof, pp. 824--825; the parity and collapse calculation for the two interval restrictions. Online paper read; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write s_i for the direction of the inequality between x_i and x_{i+1} (0\le i<w). By the alternating hypothesis, when p=- the step s_i is upward exactly for even i, and when p=+ exactly for odd i. At a boundary between two different labels, a 0-to-1 transition at k (x_k\le h<x_{k+1}) has s_k upward, and a 1-to-0 transition at k (x_k>h\ge x_{k+1}) has s_k downward. We also fix the directions at the two ends: s_0 is upward if p=- (x_0=0 is minimal) and downward if p=+ (x_0=r+1 is maximal), and, when w\geq1, s_{w-1} is downward if q=- (x_w=0 is minimal) and upward if q=+ (x_w=r+1 is maximal). The first entry has label 0 when p=- and label 1 when p=+ (as 0\le h\le r), and the last entry has label 0 when q=- and 1 when q=+. Now take a maximal run x_i,\ldots,x_k. Its length k-i+1 is odd iff k-i is even. (a) Interior run (0<i, k<w): the transitions at i-1 and k go into and out of the same label, so one is 0-to-1 and the other 1-to-0; s_{i-1} and s_k have opposite directions, hence k-(i-1) is odd and k-i is even. (b) First run with k<w: its label is that of x_0 and the transition at k leaves it, so s_k has the same direction as s_0 (0-to-1 and s_0 upward when p=-; 1-to-0 and s_0 downward when p=+); hence k is even. (c) Last run with i>0: the transition at i-1 enters the label of x_w, so s_{i-1} has the same direction as s_{w-1} (1-to-0 and s_{w-1} downward when q=-; 0-to-1 and s_{w-1} upward when q=+); hence (w-1)-(i-1)=w-i is even. (d) A single run (i=0, k=w): if w=0 the length is 1; if w\geq1, x_0 and x_w have the same label, so p=q, and s_0, s_{w-1} have opposite directions (upward then downward for p=q=-, downward then upward for p=q=+), so w-1 is odd and w is even. In all cases every maximal run has odd length.

proof.text: For a constant word of odd length, the leftmost-equal-pair reduction deletes two entries at each move and therefore leaves exactly one copy of that constant. Under C_h, every entry in a 0-run is unchanged and every entry in a 1-run becomes h+1. Thus each 1-run reduces to one h+1, while each 0-run retains all of its entries. At a run boundary the two labels differ, so one side is at most h and the other is h+1; the boundary entries are unequal and no deletion crosses the boundary. Strict inequalities inside each surviving 0-run are unchanged, so the run order and alternating directions remain as asserted for R(C_{h*}x).

source.place: Riehl--Verity, Proposition 3.2.2 proof, pp. 824--825; the parity and collapse calculation for the two interval restrictions.

proof.text: Under D_h, every entry in a 0-run becomes 0, while an entry j>h in a 1-run becomes j-h. Hence each odd 0-run reduces to one 0, and each 1-run keeps its entrywise shifted word with all strict inequalities preserved. At a boundary, a 0-side has value 0 and a 1-side has a positive value, so the boundary entries are unequal and no cancellation crosses a run. Therefore R(D_{h*}x) has exactly the stated replacements, with the original run order and alternating inequality directions unchanged.

source.place: Riehl--Verity, Proposition 3.2.2 proof, pp. 824--825; the parity and collapse calculation for the two interval restrictions.

proof.text: The preceding three calculations apply also to the first and last runs, including singleton runs. Since the reduction algorithm always deletes the leftmost adjacent equal pair and every possible equal pair lies inside one of the constant image runs, reducing the whole word is the same as reducing its runs independently in order. This proves all clauses of the statement for every 0\le h\le r, including r=0 and either endpoint sign.

lean.statement: theorem block_run_collapse (r h : ℕ) (p q : Bool) (x : List ℕ) (hx : IsWord r p q x) (hh : h ≤ r) : (∀ b ∈ thresholdRuns h x, Odd b.length) ∧ reduce (x.map (lowerRestriction h)) = (thresholdRuns h x).flatMap (lowerRun h) ∧ reduce (x.map (upperRestriction h)) = (thresholdRuns h x).flatMap (upperRun h) ∧ NoCrossRunDeletion h (lowerRestriction h) x ∧ NoCrossRunDeletion h (upperRestriction h) x ∧ IsAlternating p (reduce (x.map (lowerRestriction h))) ∧ IsAlternating p (reduce (x.map (upperRestriction h)))
